Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:41: And likewise, at his meals, in his rejoicing, on his festivals and appointed times, and in his sukkah, he [the external force] should not enter or intermingle with him - and one should invite the poor, who are a dwelling place for holiness, as is known. And one's charity should precede all one's affairs, for through that single coin holiness immediately becomes present. And one should not utter anything against Satan, nor mention him, nor cast [words] in anger, which is an offering to him, and the like. And one should not curse oneself, nor say "let it be for Satan" or "in a bad hour" and the like, for speech causes great harm. And one should not frighten a small child by saying "the cat will take you," "the camel will take you," "the dog will take you, bite him," and the like, since he [the external force] is called by the names of dog and cat and all evil names, to do harm - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:42: It remains for us to explain the times for the holiness of union, to draw down holy souls: the specific time is at midnight or after midnight - this for the rest of the people; and for Torah scholars, on Sabbath eve at midnight or after midnight - and we have already copied the words of the Zohar above, in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:43: And concerning what my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote, that the first preparation for union is a person's purification from his sins - so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Bereishit, page 54a), which we copied above in chapter 5, that just as a person is drawn, so he draws a soul for his child - and if he is drawn after holiness he draws a holy soul, and if, God forbid, he is drawn after impurity, he likewise draws, from the Other Side, an impure soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:44: And therefore, besides the repentance one must do at the time of begetting, one must precede it with repentance so that a fit wife come to him and his seed go out clean, without refuse - as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Vayechi, page 229a) on the verse, "the angel who redeems me from all evil" (Genesis 48:16) - these are its words: Rabbi Chiya opened and said (Proverbs 19:14), "house and wealth are an inheritance from fathers" - but are they truly an inheritance from fathers? Behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives everything to a person, and once a person has inherited a house and money, sometimes he shall bequeath everything to his son, and it becomes an inheritance from his fathers - but "and from the LORD, a prudent wife" - because, when a person inherits a wife, he inherits her from with the Holy One, blessed be He, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not bestow a wife on a person except when it is announced concerning her in the firmament, for the Holy One, blessed be He, pairs matches before they come into the world - and when people merit according to their deeds, they are given a wife accordingly, and everything is revealed before the Holy One, blessed be He, and according to the deeds of the meritorious, so are matches paired - and sometimes, when they [souls] ascend in the scales [for judgment], and that person strays from his way, his match is raised to another, until his deeds improve; and when his deeds improve, or his time arrives, one man is pushed aside before another, and this one comes and takes what was his - and this is difficult before the Holy One, blessed be He, more than anything, to push a man aside before another man - and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is the one who gives a wife to a person, and matches come from Him - and this is "and from the LORD, a prudent wife" - therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, gives everything to a person.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:45: And if you say, "a prudent wife" and not another - come and see: even though the Holy One, blessed be He, has prepared good things for a person to give him, and he strays from his way from with the Holy One, blessed be He, toward another side - from that other side to which he has attached himself comes to him whatever comes to him: all accusations and all evils, and they do not come to him from with the Holy One, blessed be He, but from that evil side to which he has attached himself, through the deeds he performed - and therefore, concerning a wife who is not prudent, King Solomon, peace be upon him, said of this (Ecclesiastes 7:26), "and I find more bitter than death the woman" - because it is through his own sins that a person draws her upon himself, through those deeds he performed. And when the Holy One, blessed be He, is pleased with a person because of his fitting deeds, He prepares for him a wife who is prudent, and redeems him with a redemption from the Other Side - and therefore Jacob said (Genesis 48:16), "the angel who redeems me from all evil" - that a wife from the Other Side was not prepared for me, and no disqualification befell my seed, for they are all righteous and complete in completeness, since he was redeemed from all evil, and Jacob did not attach himself to that Other Side at all - and therefore, "the angel who redeems me from all evil" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:46: Behold, a person does not merit his true match from the side of holiness until his deeds improve - like Jacob, who, because he did not attach himself to the side of evil, merited his true match and his seed went out clean without refuse - for the woman is like the earth: if a person does not sow in fitting earth, it shall not bring forth good growth, but if the earth is fit for sowing, it shall bring forth growth properly. Therefore repentance and prayer are needed, as it is said (Psalms 32:6), "for this, let every pious one pray to You at a time when You may be found" - and they, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 8a), "at a time when You may be found" - this refers to a wife. Behold, besides being pious, one needs prayer as well. And the reason is that when one has not yet encountered his true match, he must return through reincarnation until he encounters her, and thus all his labor is found to be in vain - and so it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:47: And in the Tikkunim (page 30a) it says: this sin, that a person mixes his firstborn drop [i.e. first seed] into "flesh boiled in her mother's milk" [an allusion], causes another to take his true match, and this is measure for measure - and therefore (Exodus 23:19), "the first of the firstfruits of your land you shall bring to the house of the LORD your God; you shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk" - for that child, who is a mixture, who emerges as a mixed kind from a woman not from him, is opposite him - and therefore, when he merits, "she becomes a helper" - his true match, who is a helper to him in Torah, in mitzvot, in fear, in love - a helper to him in this world and in the World to Come. But if not, another who is not from him is opposite him, to destroy him from both worlds - and all this is caused to him because he did not guard the first drop for his true match. And nevertheless, if he returns in repentance, it is said (Isaiah 6:10), "and he shall return and be healed," and he is given his true match, of whom it is said (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel" - and she is the image of Torah, which is healing and is life - this is what is written (ibid. 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who grasp it" - and the wife is in this image, this is what is written (Ecclesiastes 9:9), "see life with the wife whom you love" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:48: Further, in Tikkun 15 (page 30b) - these are its words: and the secret of the matter: whoever treats bread with contempt, the crumbs of bread, which are drops the size of an olive, poverty pursues him - rather, one must guard one's own drops, that he not cast them where they are not needed - and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established, honor your wives so that you become wealthy - and they honored them, to guard the first drop, that he not cause refuse in it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:49: It remains for us to explain the specific times for the holiness of union, to draw down holy souls: the specific time is midnight for the rest of the people, or after midnight; and for Torah scholars, on Sabbath eve at midnight or after midnight - and we have already copied the words of the Zohar above, in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:50: Further, they said in the Midrash (HaNe'elam, Parashat Vayera, page 112a) - these are its words: Rabbi Yosef, when he went down to Babylon, saw those young unmarried men who would go in among beautiful women and not sin - he said to them, are you not afraid of the evil inclination? They said, we do not come from an unholy conception; we were circumcised from a holy sanctification, for Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, a person must sanctify himself at the time of relations, and from him come forth holy children, worthy children, who are not afraid of the evil inclination, as it is said (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy." Rabbi Abba said, what is meant by (Ezekiel 20:20), "and sanctify My Sabbaths"? Rather, the conjugal time of Torah scholars is only from Sabbath to Sabbath, and it warns them: since the conjugal act is a mitzvah, sanctify it - meaning, sanctify yourselves on My Sabbaths in that conjugal act which is a mitzvah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:51: And they were strict in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria, page 49b) concerning one who does not observe this holiness, and it said that one who unites with his wife before midnight draws a soul from the Other Side, and of him it is said (Proverbs 19:2), "also, without knowledge, the soul is not good," and likewise, "and he who hurries with his feet sins" - and it said, whoever hurries and rushes the hour without holy desire certainly sins in everything. And it said that of this it is said (Psalms 32:9), "be not like a horse or mule without understanding," and it said, in what are people distinguished from a horse and a mule? In the holiness of themselves, to be found complete and marked apart from everything - and it said that of this the Torah commanded, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" - if they distance themselves [from this practice], where is their holiness? And for this one must rebuke his inclination, and if thoughts come, he should nullify them with words of Torah, which is the antidote to the evil inclination, and remember for it the day of death. And nevertheless one must be cunning in fear: if he sees that his inclination shall overpower him and he shall come to emit seed in vain, it is better that he transgress a positive commandment than a prohibition, which is called "evil" and liable for death and the other punishments to be explained in their place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:52: Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Bereishit, page 49b) the fitting times for union - these are its words: Rabbi Shimon opened and said, "and he went on his journeys [lemasa'av] from the south as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai" (Genesis 13:3) - "and he went on his journeys" - it should have said "on his journey" [singular]; what is "on his journeys"? Rather, there are two journeys, one his own and one the Shechinah's, for every person must be found male and female, in order to strengthen faith, and then the Shechinah never separates from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:53: And if you say, one who goes out on the road, where male and female are not found together, does the Shechinah separate from him? Come and see: this one who goes out on the road and arranges his prayer before the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to draw upon himself the Shechinah of his Master, before he goes out at the time male and female were found together - once he has arranged his prayer and his praise and his Shechinah rests upon him, he may go out, for the Shechinah unites with him so that male and female be found: male and female in the town, male and female in the field - this is what is written (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness shall go before him, and shall make his footsteps a way."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:54: Come and see, all the time a person is delayed on the road he must guard his deeds, since the supernal union does not separate from him, lest a blemish be found without male and female. In the town, this is needed when his wife is with him, and all the more so here [on the road], for the supernal union is bound to him - and moreover, that union guards him on his road and does not separate from him until he returns home. At the hour he enters his house, he must gladden his house, since his house caused him that supernal union - once he comes to her he must gladden her, for two reasons: one, for the joy of that union, since it is the joy of a mitzvah, the joy of the Shechinah; and moreover, that it increases peace below - this is what is written (Job 5:24), "and you shall know that peace is your tent; you shall visit your abode and not sin" - and does not visiting his wife constitute sin? So it is indeed, since he diminishes the honor of the supernal union that united with him, which his wife caused him. And one - that if his wife conceives, the supernal union pours a holy soul into it, for this covenant is called the covenant of the Holy One, blessed be He. And therefore one must intend this joy just as one must intend the joy of the Sabbath, which the wise ones know - and therefore, "and you shall know that peace is your tent," for the Shechinah comes with you and dwells in your house - and therefore, "and you shall visit your abode and not sin" - what is "and not sin"? To serve before the Holy One, blessed be He, with the joy of a mitzvah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:55: In this manner, Torah scholars who separate from their wives all the days of the week in order to occupy themselves with Torah - the supernal union unites with them and does not separate from them, since they are found as male and female [in a spiritual sense]; when the Sabbath enters, the Torah scholars must gladden their houses, for the honor of the supernal union, and direct their hearts with the desire of their Master, as stated.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:56: In this manner, one whose wife is in her days of impurity, and he guards her properly - all those days the supernal union unites with him and male and female are found, since, once his wife is purified, he must gladden her with the joy of a mitzvah, a supernal joy. And all these reasons we have stated ascend to one level: put simply, all those people of faith must direct their heart and desire to this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:57: Further, concerning the union of a man with his wife, what Rabbeinu Moshe ben Nachman, of blessed memory, composed (Iggeret HaKodesh): know that since the nation of Israel is unified to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He set them apart, through His holy Torah, from all the nations who worship idols - just as He, blessed be He, is [set apart] from all besides Him, as He, blessed be He, said (Isaiah 43:21), "this people I formed for Myself," and so on, and He said elsewhere, "the LORD is one," by way of equivalence - and this is what we say (the Sabbath Minchah prayer), "You are One and Your Name is One, and who is like Your people Israel, a nation one [in the earth]." And afterward it said, "I formed for Myself," meaning, I set apart for Myself, to be unified for My glory, as He said (Leviticus 20:26), "and I have set you apart from the peoples to be Mine."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:58: And you already know that servants conduct themselves according to what they see in the conduct of their master - and He, blessed be He, who is our Master and we His servants, is holy, and there is none holy like Him, and He commanded us to be holy as He is holy - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained on the verse (Deuteronomy 28:9), "and you shall walk in His ways" - just as He is holy, so you shall be holy; just as He is gracious, so you shall be gracious. If so, all of Israel's conduct is found founded on the unification of the great Name, blessed be He - therefore they resemble Him in all their deeds - and He, blessed be He, said (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" - and since all our deeds are in the likeness of the deeds of the Name, blessed be He, it follows that whenever we do what is good and upright, we sanctify His great Name, as He said (Deuteronomy 4:8), "and what great nation is there that has statutes," and so on - because we resemble our Creator, blessed be He; and whenever we do not conduct ourselves properly and all our deeds are corrupted, we profane the Name of Heaven through them, since we resemble Him, and our deeds are ugly. And of this they said in Tractate Yoma (86a), when a person reads [Scripture] and studies [Mishnah] and his business dealings are conducted faithfully, of him Scripture says (Isaiah 49:3), "and He said to me, you are My servant," and so on - but when a person reads and studies and his business dealings are not conducted faithfully, what do people say of him? Have you seen so-and-so, how corrupted are his ways and his deeds - and of him Scripture says (Jeremiah 34:20 / cf. Ezekiel 36:20), "these are the people of the LORD, and they have gone forth from His land" - and the Name of Heaven is found profaned. And the reason for all this that we have said is that since we resemble Him in our deeds, the sanctification of the Name or its profanation depends on our deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:59: And after we have made all this known to you, know that since man's matter and his nature are the cause of his being evil or good, from the aspect of the constitution of the mixture according to the drop from which he came into being, and his union is found to be the cause of the sanctification of the Name or its profanation according to the children he begets - He commanded us concerning this and warned us, saying that we must sanctify ourselves at the time of relations, as the tradition came in the verse (Leviticus 15:31), "and you shall set apart the children of Israel [from their impurity]" - and because this is a cause for a person to beget righteous children who sanctify the Name of Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:60: And since the matter is so, you need to know what we have said, that a person must sanctify himself at the time of relations, and this holiness is divided into five parts: the first way concerns the essence of the union; the second way concerns the timing of the union; the third way concerns the food fit for union; the fourth way concerns the intent of union; the fifth way concerns the manner of the union. And I now proceed to explain these matters in a way that shall suffice, according to the intent proper to each one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:61: The first way, concerning the essence of the union:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:62: Know that this union is a holy and clean matter when the thing is done as is fitting, at the fitting time, and with proper intent - and let no one think that in proper union there is disgrace or ugliness, God forbid, for proper union is called "knowledge" [da'at], and it is not for nothing that it is called so (I Samuel 1:19), "and Elkanah knew Chanah his wife," and so on - and this is the secret of the drop of seed, when it is drawn from the place of Da'at and Binah, which is the brain. And know that were there not great holiness in this matter, they would not call union "knowledge." And the Name, blessed be He, created everything as His wisdom decreed, and did not create anything that would be disgraceful or ugly - for if one were to say that union is a disgraceful thing, then the organs of intercourse are organs of disgrace, and behold, the Name, blessed be He, created them by His word, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "He made you and established you" - and they, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Chullin (56b), that the Holy One, blessed be He, created "settings" [konaniyot] in man. And in Midrash Ecclesiastes (2:15) they said, on "which has already been made" (Ecclesiastes 2:12) - this teaches that He and His court took a count of every single organ and set it in its place. And if the organs of intercourse were disgraceful organs, how could the Name, blessed be He, have created a thing having deficiency or disgrace, Heaven forfend? Rather, the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, are perfect, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:4), "the Rock, His work is perfect" - and the Name, blessed be He, is "of eyes too pure to behold evil" (Habakkuk 1:13); before Him there is no matter of corruption or disgrace - and He created man and woman, and created every single organ within them and prepared them according to their proper arrangement, and did not create in them anything disgraceful.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:63: And the clear proof is what is said concerning the account of Creation (Genesis 2:25), "and the two of them were naked," and so on - all this before they sinned, because they were occupied with intellectual matters and all their intent was toward Heaven, and their eyes regarded these organs no differently than the eyes or the other organs of the body; but when they turned after bodily pleasures and did not intend for the sake of Heaven, it says (ibid. 3:7), "and they knew that they were naked." And its explanation is that just as hands, at the time they write a Torah scroll in purity, are honored and praiseworthy, but when they steal or do a disgraceful thing they are disgraceful - so are the organs of intercourse for a man and his wife before they sinned; and just as there is, in every single organ, praise and honor in doing good, and disgrace in doing evil, so it was for Adam in the organs of intercourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:64: It follows that all the Holy One, blessed be He's ways are justice, purity, and cleanliness, and all the ugliness is found to be entirely from the side of man's action - of this Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:29), "only see this have I found, that God made man upright," and so on - meaning, in none of the organs of man, from the aspect of creation, is there any corruption or ugliness, for everything, in supernal wisdom, is a fixed, good, and pleasant matter; but man, in his folly, brings ugliness into things that had no ugliness at first - understand this well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:65: Now, the secret of "knowledge" that I hint to you is the secret of man being included in the secret of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at, for man is the secret of Da'at, and this is the secret of man and woman in the secret of the inner tradition - and if so, the matter of union is a matter of great elevation, when done properly. And they, of blessed memory, said, at the time a man unites with his wife in holiness, the Shechinah rests between them - the secret of man [ish] and woman [ishah]: when they are warmed [in holiness], the letters Yud and Hei [of the divine Name] are present between them; when the Shechinah departs from between them, only fire and fire remain - as we learn in Sotah (17a), Rabbi Akiva used to expound: man and woman, if they merit, the Shechinah is between them; if they do not merit, fire consumes them. Explanation: when a man unites with his wife in holiness, the Shechinah is between them - you find in the name "ish" [man] a Yud, and in the name "ishah" [woman] a Hei - behold, this is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, found between them; but if they did not intend a holy union but only to fill their desire, and through desire and lust they became warmed with fire, the Yud of the name of the man and the Hei of the name of the woman, which are Yud-Hei, depart from between them, and only fire and fire remain. And it is to this secret that they, of blessed memory, intended in saying (Niddah 31a), there are three partners in a person, and they are: man, woman, and the Holy One, blessed be He - and if the matter were disgraceful, how could they include the Name, blessed be He, in a matter that is so?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:66: Now, the Name, blessed be He, said to Abraham concerning the birth of Isaac, "and I will bless her, and I will also give you a son from her" (Genesis 17:16), and concerning Rebecca, "and Isaac entreated the LORD," and so on (ibid. 25:21), and concerning Rachel and Leah, "and He opened her womb" (ibid. 29:31, 30:22), and concerning Elkanah and so on - and behold, among the general blessings, "there shall be none bereaved or barren" (Exodus 23:26). And further, we learn in Chagigah, three keys were not given into the hand of an agent, and one of them is childbirth, as it is said, "and He opened her womb," and so on - and if the matter were disgraceful, why would the Holy One, blessed be He, do it without an agent?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:67: And in Bereishit Rabbah (85:8), on "and he turned aside to her by the road" (Genesis 38:16) - Judah sought to pass by, [but] the Holy One, blessed be He, signaled to the angel appointed over desire - this comes to make known that the intent and desire of the Name, blessed be He, was in this union, and therefore both of them were born twins, both righteous, both pure, in the likeness of sun and moon, Peretz and Zerach - and understand, that they were born as the form of the orders of the world, and there is no disgrace in their union, just as there is no disgrace in the arrangement of the orders of the world, in general and in particular.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:68: And concerning Ruth it is said (Ruth 4:13), "and the LORD gave her conception," and so on - and if there were disgrace in the matter, it has already been said, "of eyes too pure to behold evil" (Habakkuk 1:13). Rather, when the union is for the sake of Heaven, there is no holier and cleaner thing above it - and therefore it is said, concerning the union of the righteous, (Jeremiah 1:5), "before I formed you in the belly, I knew you," and so on. But in the union of the wicked and lawless, that entire drop is impure, the Name has no portion in it, and of it is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb." But concerning the union of a man with his wife properly, they, of blessed memory, explained that it is like the likeness of heaven and earth, as it is said (Zechariah 12:1), "the utterance of the LORD, who stretches out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth and forms the spirit of man within him," and it says (Amos 9:6), "and has founded His vault upon the earth" - they are one bundle to create man. And this is "let us make man in our image" (Genesis 1:26) - meaning, I too am a partner in the creation of man - and this partnership is that from the father and mother all the orders of the body are drawn, and the Name, blessed be He, casts into it a soul, as He said (ibid. 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life," and it says (Ecclesiastes 12:7), "and the dust returns to the earth as it was," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:69: And after we have made known to you the secret of the first way of union, we shall make known to you the second way, which is the opposite of the first: for when a person does not intend for the sake of Heaven, that seed drawn forth is a foul drop, in which the Name has no portion, and it is called "one who corrupts his way upon the earth" - and his whole body is [given] to haste, and it is as though he plants an Asherah and fattens calves for idolatry, since it is a corrupted seed and a drop cast into a repulsive channel - and of him it is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb" - and behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah and said (Leviticus 20:26), "and you shall be holy to Me," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:70: The second Gate, concerning the timing of union:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:71: Now, the Name, blessed be He, said in the Torah (Exodus 21:10), "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" - and the conjugal right [onah] mentioned in the Torah is spelled out in the Gemara (Ketubot 61b), for the conjugal times vary according to the occupation of each person. And now we shall set aside speaking of the conjugal times of the rest of the people, and speak of the fitting conjugal time of Torah scholars, which is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve - and of this it is said (Psalms 1:3), "who yields his fruit in its season," and so on - this is the conjugal time of Torah scholars (see Ketubot 62b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:72: And know, a man's seed is the life of his body and the light of its radiance, for it is the choicest and purest blood in the body - for were this not so, the form of man would not be in it. Now, the seed is from parts of the body, and has a part from every single organ, for it is known that an ear is not born from an eye, nor an eye from an ear, but rather every organ is drawn from the nature of a similar organ - just as beans and lentils do not grow from wheat seed, nor a donkey or ox or sheep from human seed - and every single organ and every single form has a specific nature and a known power from which it is born; and one need not worry about a blind man begetting a sighted one, for the organ's power is found within the general nature of the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:73: And if so, the seed is a part of every single organ of the organs of the body, and it is not fitting for a person to be found with his wife like a rooster, for then his strength would weaken and the light of his eyes diminish, and all the portions of his organs would become depleted - but when the union is at the known conjugal time, which is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, which is the secret of the turning of the spheres, front and back, over the seven days of the week - then he can bestow strength on another and he himself shall lack nothing, that a visible weakness come upon him, since he has already received strength that he can bestow from - and therefore it says (Psalms 1:3), "who yields his fruit in its season" - namely from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve - and juxtaposed to it, "and his leaf shall not wither," meaning the union shall be for the sake of Heaven and come to a complete deed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:74: And the reason it is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve is that the Sabbath is the foundation of the world and is the likeness of the world of souls, for the reason of "Shabbat LaShem" - and Torah scholars intended, from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, to beget a form fit for the service of the Creator, blessed be He, possessing a pure, supernal, intellectual soul, as He said (Exodus 31:17), "and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed [vayinafash]." And this is the intent behind the conjugal time of Torah scholars - understand this well - for they did not set their conjugal time on the days of physicality, namely the six days of labor, but rather on the day that is entirely Sabbath and the world of souls.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:75: And after we have aroused you to this, let us return to what was our intent to arrange: that the timing of union is divided into three parts - the first part, the conjugal time by days; the second, the conjugal time from the aspect of food; the third, the conjugal time from the aspect of the hours. Now, the first part we have already explained in this chapter; the second of the three parts, which is the conjugal time from the aspect of food, you shall need to know, God willing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:76: Know that the food by which a person is nourished requires three kinds of transformation, and at the fourth level it turns into seed or into white blood that sustains the body - and if a person has relations soon after eating, then at that time the nature of the body is boiling, and the blood is mixed and not pure and clear, and that drop drawn from him is murky and soiled, foul and filthy, not clean or pure - and it follows that the offspring from that drop is from a murky and filthy foundation, and of it is said (Job 15:35), "they conceive mischief and bring forth iniquity," and it says (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb" - because the nature of the constitution of a drop that is not pure necessitates that what is formed from it be repulsive and filthy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:77: Therefore a person must time the union for an hour when his soul is settled upon him, and the nature of the body has quieted from the boiling of the food he ate, and the blood has been refined and the rains have descended to their natural place - and then the elements of a person's body are arranged in proper order, which is preserved for the latter half of the night. And of this they, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Berachot (5b): Abba Binyamin says, all my days I was troubled about two things: about my bed, that it be placed between north and south, and so on - and Rabbi Yitzchak said, one who places his bed between north and south shall have male children, as it is said (Psalms 17:14), "and Your treasure [tzefunecha] shall fill their belly; they shall be satisfied with sons," and so on. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, also his wife shall not miscarry - it is written here, "shall fill," and it is written there (Genesis 25:24), "and her days were filled to give birth," and so on. And I must arouse you concerning this teaching: it is known that there is no fool or simpleton in the world who supposes that because of the placement of the bed between north and south a person merits male children, and that his wife shall not miscarry - all the more so that the pillars of the world, wise and understanding men, would say such things. Rather, they spoke these words as allusions, according to their good custom everywhere, and I shall explain: it is known that intense cold is toward the northern direction, and intense heat toward the southern direction, and the sages of truth know that a person's inclining toward the extremes is not the way of what is good and upright, but the moderate attributes are the choicest - and of this Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:16-17), "be not overly righteous, and be not overly wicked, and be not a fool" - and since north and south are the two opposites for heat and cold, they concealed their words and hinted them, saying that one who has relations while his body's constitution is balanced between heat and cold - then his natural faculties can rest and he shall not emit quickly, but rather can have intercourse and wait, and then the woman emits first, and the woman's seed is found to be like the likeness of matter, and when the man's seed comes afterward, it is found to be like the likeness of the sculptor who forms a shape in matter - and this is the secret of what they, of blessed memory, said (see Niddah 71a), as a reward for the righteous delaying [emission] upon the woman's belly, they have male children, as it is said (Psalms 127:3), "behold, sons are the heritage of the LORD," and so on. And once you understand all this, you shall understand the secret of "one who places his bed between north and south shall have male children" - this is found in the middle of the night, when the body has already quieted from the boiling of the nature of the food eaten, and the body's constitution is clear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:78: And what it said, "between north and south," between cold and heat - it is known that every man born from a cold drop shall always be a simpleton and a fool, and one born from a hot drop shall be a man of wrath and anger, but one born from a drop balanced between heat and cold shall always be wise, precious of spirit, a man of understanding, and shall be, in his opinions, moderate among people - and of this it is said (I Samuel 1:11), "and give Your maidservant seed of men." And what they, of blessed memory, expounded in Gemara Berachot (31b), "neither dark nor fair, [neither wise] nor foolish, neither tall nor short" - for all the [balanced] attributes come to be in a person when his constitution is between cold and heat, which is the secret of "between north and south," and this is the secret of male children that we have spoken of.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:79: But what they said, that his wife shall not miscarry, there is in this matter a complete principle, and I shall now open for you gates of light on this. You already know what they, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 82b) concerning that pregnant woman who smelled [food on Yom Kippur], and so on - "they whispered to her, and it was whispered" - this is [balanced,] between north and south - of her Scripture says (Jeremiah 1:5), "before I formed you in the belly," and so on; but that pregnant woman for whom "they whispered and it was not whispered [i.e., she was not satisfied]" - this leans toward the southern direction - of her Scripture says (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb." And it is known that the cause of miscarriage is when the womb is aroused toward one of the extremes - whether toward hunger or toward desire she miscarries, whether toward heat or toward cold - for when the womb is balanced, it shall never miscarry, like a scale in the eye of justice, that the balances not tilt to either side; and if so, one "for whom it was whispered and it was not whispered" leans from the middle extreme, and is close to becoming a miscarriage if she is not fed from what she smelled. And if you say, behold, even if the righteous woman smelled - although she smelled, she still returned to the middle balance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:80: If so, understand and contemplate the time fitting for a person to have relations, and you shall merit children fit for [rendering] instruction. And behold, we have summarized in this way three times for the conjugal duty: from the aspect of days, from the aspect of food, and from the aspect of the hours.
